title: Slower production growth will push copper market to deficit in 2026, says ICSG | Reuters
text:
Slower production growth will push copper market to deficit in 2026, says ICSG | Reuters

A coil of copper rod sits on the production line for copper flat wire at the Wellascent factory in Ganzhou, Jiangxi province, China August 14, 2025. REUTERS/Florence Lo Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab

LONDON, Oct 8 (Reuters) - The global refined copper market is expected to swing to a deficit of 150,000 metric tons in 2026 from the previously expected surplus of 209,000 tons due to slower production growth, the International Copper Study Group (ICSG) said.

Copper prices briefly hit a 16-month peak on Wednesday due to worries about potential shortages from a series of recent mine disruptions in Indonesia, Chile and Congo.

These incidents prompted the ICSG to revise down its forecast for the 2025 global mine production growth to 1.4% from 2.3% it expected in April, it said in a statement on We
